transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, do you have a moment for us to talk?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do, but I'm just really worried about when I can get home. My kids are with my sister and I can't stay there forever.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. First, I want to say that I am very sorry. I made a mistake in how I managed your baby's monitoring earlier today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I looked at the fetal heart rate tracing and I didn't categorize the decelerations correctly. I missed the severity of what was happening on the monitor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, you missed something? Was the baby okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: A second doctor reviewed the trace two hours later and identified that it should have been flagged as more urgent. I take full responsibility for this. I am so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Two hours? You left it for two hours? Oh my god, is the baby alright? Is that why things were so stressful?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable now, but that delay was my fault. I apologize deeply for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I'm already terrified about how I'm going to manage two kids and this recovery, and now I find out you just missed something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is incredibly overwhelming.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not just overwhelming, it's scary. I'm sitting here wondering if my baby is permanently hurt because you weren't looking properly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're scared.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm more than scared. I'm thinking about my children. If something happened to the baby, my life would be over. Do you even understand how much is on my plate right now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're under a lot of pressure. Look, I really need to get to another patient who is crashing, so I have to be quick.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have to be quick? I just found out you messed up my baby's care and you're rushing off?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry for the error and I feel terrible about it. I just have a clinical emergency in the next room.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. So what now? Is my baby actually okay or are you just saying that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is currently stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't answer my question. What is the actual plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to keep the monitoring running.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's it? Just keep monitoring?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, we'll keep a close eye on the heart rate for the next few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? When can I go home? I told you, I can't stay here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the next few readings go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand why this happened. How do you just miss a heart rate?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the categorization of the dips in the heart rate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? You just said you made a mistake. Now it's confusion?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize. It was my error. I let the timing slip.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I can't even trust you. How am I supposed to trust anyone in this ward now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand why you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to call my sister. I need to tell her what's happening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Of course, you should do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are there other doctors who are going to check the monitor? Or is it just you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Another clinician will be reviewing the traces periodically.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How often?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Every so often.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an answer. Every hour? Every ten minutes?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll maintain the standard protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just not enough. I need to know my baby is safe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've given you the most accurate information I have right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just so overwhelmed. I don't know what to do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I really do have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Just go then. Just leave.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to be quick', 'I really do have to go now') and prioritizes their schedule over the patient's distress.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and early, but there were no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language and took full personal responsibility ('I take full responsibility', 'my fault') without deflecting.

R.justification: Resident named specific emotions ('scared', 'under a lot of pressure') and engaged with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan was vague ('keep the monitoring running', 'standard protocol') with no specific timelines or patient role defined.
